answer: Cloth masks provide minimal protection against PM2.5 and should not be relied upon during hazardous smog days. Use an N95 or KN95 mask instead, properly fitted with a seal around the nose and mouth, to filter PM2.5 effectively (DOC-12).

During a smog alert, when forecast PM2.5 reaches 165 µg/m³ or above, brick kilns without approved emission-control technology must suspend operations (DOC-08). Industries must also report stack emissions data daily to the Department during smog alerts. These restrictions are lifted when forecast PM2.5 stays below 165 µg/m³ for two consecutive days.

Under the 2023 regulations (DOC-02), schools closed only when PM2.5 exceeded 300 µg/m³ for two consecutive days; there was no half-day closure provision. DOC-02 was superseded by DOC-03, effective 2026-09-20. Under the current rule, schools close fully when forecast PM2.5 is 250 µg/m³ or above, and switch to half-days, closing by 12:00 PM, when forecast PM2.5 is 165–249 µg/m³.
